teachingCards.title: Historical Origin
teachingCards.content: A military image: armies sometimes burned bridges behind them to prevent retreat — making the path back impossible.

teachingCards.title: Natural Usage
teachingCards.content: "Even though he was frustrated, he was careful not to burn bridges with his old team."

quests.word: GIVE THE BENEFIT OF THE DOUBT
quests.conceptTitle: Idiom Anatomy: GIVE THE BENEFIT OF THE DOUBT
quests.definition: 'Give the benefit of the doubt' means to trust someone's honesty or intentions even without full proof.
quests.example: He was late again, but I gave him the benefit of the doubt since traffic was terrible.
quests.exampleSentence: He was late again, but I gave him the benefit of the doubt since traffic was terrible.
quests.contextSentence: He was late again, but I gave him the benefit of the doubt since traffic was terrible.
quests.origin: A legal phrase originally, related to the principle that uncertainty should favor the accused rather than assume guilt.

quests.word: CROSS THAT BRIDGE WHEN WE COME TO IT
quests.conceptTitle: Idiom Anatomy: CROSS THAT BRIDGE WHEN WE COME TO IT
quests.definition: 'Cross that bridge when we come to it' means to postpone worrying about a hypothetical problem until it actually arises.
quests.example: What if they say no?" "Let's cross that bridge when we come to it.
quests.exampleSentence: What if they say no?" "Let's cross that bridge when we come to it.
quests.contextSentence: What if they say no?" "Let's cross that bridge when we come to it.
quests.origin: A literal travel image: there's no point planning how to cross a bridge you haven't reached yet.
